title: A Grand Day Out
format: Six posters, a social series, and a 15-second spot
summary: A campaign that makes people want to go somewhere. Posters, social posts, and a short spot that sell a day trip to the moon like an old seaside holiday.
coverAlt: Vintage-style travel poster of a picnic on the grey sand of the moon

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Old railway posters sold the seaside with one picture and one line. The moon gets the same treatment. Sun, sand, and a picnic, except the sand is grey and the picnic is cheese.

blocks.label: Research. Railway and seaside posters from the 1920s to the 1950s, sorted by how few words they used.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: I wrote the lines before drawing anything, and kept only those that worked without a picture. Each poster then got one image and one line. The social posts and the spot reuse the same pictures, so the campaign looks the same wherever people meet it.

blocks.caption: From the headline tests to the final poster.
The six posters, shown together at a station.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: Restraint did more work than any illustration. Next time I would test the lines with strangers, not classmates, who already knew the joke.
